sources.title: Post-quantum Cryptography
Energy Consumption of Post-Quantum Cryptography on Constrained and General-Purpose Architectures
sources.venue: Gillot, O., Buchanan, W. J., & Tehrani, M. G. (2026). Energy Consumption of Post-Quantum Cryptography on Constrained and General-Purpose Architectures. Cryptography, 10(4), 55
sources.abstract: With Q-day approaching, the transition to post-quantum cryptography (PQC) has begun, with governments across the US, UK and EU mandating migration to quantum-resistant standards. This paper benchmarks the three NIST-standardised PQC algorithms - FIPS 203 (ML-KEM), FIPS 204 (ML-DSA) and FIPS 205 (SLH-DSA) - across key generation, signing and verification operations, measuring both computational performance and energy consumption on a range of constrained IoT-class devices, from the 32-bit Raspberry Pi 1 and Zero to the 64-bit Raspberry Pi 4, as well as commodity laptop hardware. Using the FNIRSI FNB58 USB power meter and OpenSSL~3.5, results show that ML-KEM and ML-DSA achieve energy and speed efficiency comparable to classical elliptic-curve cryptography across all tested architectures. However, SLH-DSA signing is inadvisable on constrained hardware: energy costs for SLH-DSA signing on 32-bit devices were up to 243\% higher than on equivalent 64-bit hardware, making it impractical for resource-limited IoT deployments. These findings have direct implications for IoT security practitioners planning PQC migration.

sources.title: A Survey of Post-Quantum Cryptography: Start of a New Race
sources.abstract: Information security is a fundamental and urgent issue in the digital transformation era. Cryptographic techniques and digital signatures have been applied to protect and authenticate relevant information. However, with the advent of quantum computers and quantum algorithms, classical cryptographic techniques have been in danger of collapsing because quantum computers can solve complex problems in polynomial time. Stemming from that risk, researchers worldwide have stepped up research on post-quantum algorithms to resist attack by quantum computers. In this review paper, we survey studies in recent years on post-quantum cryptography (PQC) and provide statistics on the number and content of publications, including a literature overview, detailed explanations of the most common methods so far, current implementation status, implementation comparisons, and discussion on future work. These studies focused on essential public cryptography techniques and digital signature schemes, and the US National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) launched a competition to select the best candidate for the expected standard. Recent studies have practically implemented the public key encryption/key encapsulation mechanism (PKE/KEM) and digital signature schemes on different hardware platforms and applied various optimization measures based on other criteria. Along with the increasing number of scientific publications, the recent trend of PQC research is increasingly evident and is the general trend in the cryptography industry. The movement opens up a promising avenue for researchers in public key cryptography and digital signatures, especially on algorithms selected by NIST.

sources.title: A Comparative Performance Evaluation of Kyber, sntrup761, and FrodoKEM for Post-Quantum Cryptography
sources.abstract: Post-quantum cryptography (PQC) aims to develop cryptographic algorithms that are secure against attacks from quantum computers. This paper compares the leading postquantum cryptographic algorithms, such as Kyber, sntrup761, and FrodoKEM, in terms of their security, performance, and real-world applicability. The review highlights the strengths and weaknesses of each algorithm and provides insights into future research directions. We also discuss the challenges of transitioning from classical to post-quantum systems and the potential impacts on various industries. This paper serves as a foundation for understanding the current state of post-quantum cryptography and its future prospects in the quantum computing era.

sources.title: Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards
A Survey on Post-Quantum Cryptography: State-of-the-Art and Challenges
sources.abstract: The paper explains that post-quantum cryptography is necessary due to the introduction of quantum computing causing certain algorithms to be broken. We analyze the different types of post-quantum cryptography, quantum cryptography and quantum-resistant cryptography, to provide a thorough understanding of the current solutions to the problems and their limitations. We explain the current state of quantum computing and how it has changed over time while discussing possible attacks on both types of post-quantum cryptography. Next, current post-quantum algorithms are discussed, and implementations are demonstrated. Lastly, we conclude that due to quantum cryptography's present limitations it is not a viable solution like it is often presented to be and that it is currently better to use quantum-resistant cryptography.

sources.title: Post Quantum Cryptography: A Review of Techniques, Challenges and Standardizations
sources.abstract: The development of large quantum computers will have dire consequences for cryptography. Most of the symmetric and asymmetric cryptographic algorithms are vulnerable to quantum algorithms. Grover’s search algorithm gives a square root time boost for the searching of the key in symmetric schemes like AES and 3DES. The security of asymmetric algorithms like RSA, Diffie Hellman, and ECC is based on the mathematical hardness of prime factorization and discrete logarithms. The best classical algorithms available take exponential time. Shor’s factoring algorithm can solve the problems in polynomial time. Major breakthroughs in quantum computing will render all the present-day widely used asymmetric cryptosystems insecure. This paper analyzes the vulnerability of the classical cryptosystems in the context of quantum computers, discusses various post-quantum cryptosystem families, discusses the status of the NIST post-quantum cryptography standardization process, provides a performance comparison of post-quantum cryptography (PQC) algorithms on different platforms, and finally provides a couple of future research directions in this field.

sources.title: The Mathematical Foundation of Post-Quantum Cryptography
sources.abstract: On July 5, 2022, the National Institute of Standards and Technology announced four possible post-quantum cryptography standards, three of them are based on lattice theory and the other one is based on Hash function. It is well-known that the security of the lattice cryptography relies on the hardness of the shortest vector problem (SVP) and the closest vector problem (CVP). In fact, the SVP is a sphere packing problem and the CVP is a sphere covering problem. Furthermore, both SVP and CVP are equivalent to arithmetic problems of positive definite quadratic forms. This paper will briefly introduce the post-quantum cryptography and show its connections with sphere packing, sphere covering, and positive definite quadratic forms.

sources.title: Post-quantum cryptography and the quantum future of cybersecurity
sources.abstract: We review the current status of efforts to develop and deploy post-quantum cryptography on the Internet. Then we suggest specific ways in which quantum technologies might be used to enhance cybersecurity in the near future and beyond. We focus on two goals: protecting the secret keys that are used in classical cryptography, and ensuring the trustworthiness of quantum computations. These goals may soon be within reach, thanks to recent progress in both theory and experiment. This progress includes interactive protocols for testing quantumness as well as for performing uncloneable cryptographic computations; and experimental demonstrations of device-independent random number generators, device-independent quantum key distribution, quantum memories, and analog quantum simulators.

sources.title: Obfuscated Quantum and Post-Quantum Cryptography
sources.venue: IEEE International Conference on Quantum Communications, Networking, and Computing (QCNC) 2026 Kobe, Japan
sources.abstract: In this work, we present an experimental deployment of a new design for combined quantum key distribution (QKD) and post-quantum cryptography (PQC). Novel to our system is the dynamic obfuscation of the QKD-PQC sequence of operations, the number of operations, and parameters related to the operations; coupled to the integration of a GPS-free quantum synchronization protocol within the QKD process. We compare the performance and overhead of our QKD-PQC system relative to a standard QKD system with one-time pad encryption, demonstrating that our design can operate in real time with little additional overhead caused by the new security features. Since our system can offer additional defensive strategies against a wide spectrum of practical attacks that undermine deployed QKD, PQC, and certain combinations of these two primitives, we suggest that our design represents one of the most secure communication systems currently available. Given the dynamic nature of its obfuscation attributes, our new system can also be adapted in the field to defeat yet-to-be-discovered practical attacks.

sources.title: Applications of Post-Quantum Cryptography
sources.venue: European Conference on Cyber Warfare and Security
sources.abstract: With the constantly advancing capabilities of quantum computers, conventional cryptographic systems relying on complex math problems may encounter unforeseen vulnerabilities. Unlike regular computers, which are often deemed cost-ineffective in cryptographic attacks, quantum computers have a significant advantage in calculation speed. This distinction potentially makes currently used algorithms less secure or even completely vulnerable, compelling the exploration of post-quantum cryptography (PQC) as the most reasonable solution to quantum threats. This review aims to provide current information on applications, benefits, and challenges associated with the PQC. The review employs a systematic scoping review with the scope restricted to the years 2022 and 2023; only articles that were published in scientific journals were used in this paper. The review examined the articles on the applications of quantum computing in various spheres. However, the scope of this paper was restricted to the domain of the PQC because most of the analyzed articles featured this field. Subsequently, the paper is analyzing various PQC algorithms, including lattice-based, hash-based, code-based, multivariate polynomial, and isogeny-based cryptography. Each algorithm is being judged based on its potential applications, robustness, and challenges. All the analyzed algorithms are promising for the post-quantum era in such applications as digital signatures, communication channels, and IoT. Moreover, some of the algorithms are already implemented in the spheres of banking transactions, communication, and intellectual property. Meanwhile, despite their potential, these algorithms face serious challenges since they lack standardization, require vast amounts of storage and computation power, and might have unknown vulnerabilities that can be discovered only with years of cryptanalysis. This overview aims to give a basic understanding of the current state of post-quantum cryptography with its applications and challenges. As the world enters the quantum era, this review not only shows the need for strong security methods that can resist quantum attacks but also presents an optimistic outlook on the future of secure communications, guided by advancements in quantum technology. By bridging the gap between theoretical research and practical implementation, this paper aims to inspire further innovation and collaboration in the field.

sources.title: Post-Quantum Cryptography Neural Network
sources.abstract: In recent years, quantum computers and Shor quantum algorithm have posed a threat to current mainstream asymmetric cryptography methods (e.g. RSA and Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC)). Therefore, it is necessary to construct a Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) method to resist quantum computing attacks. Therefore, this study proposes a PQC-based neural network that maps a code-based PQC method to a neural network structure and enhances the security of ciphertexts with non-linear activation functions, random perturbation of ciphertexts, and uniform distribution of ciphertexts. In practical experiments, this study uses cellular network signals as a case study to demonstrate that encryption and decryption can be performed by the proposed PQC-based neural network with the uniform distribution of ciphertexts. In the future, the proposed PQC-based neural network could be applied to various applications.

sources.title: Fundamental Limitations of Post-Quantum Cryptographic Architectures
sources.abstract: Modern lattice-based cryptography, particularly the learning with errors paradigm, relies on injecting artificial noise to secure data against quantum adversaries. This study systematically examines the theoretical and physical boundaries of this noise-reliant model across four interconnected domains: computational complexity, information-theoretic thermodynamics, quantum error correction, and quantum learning theory. Starting from the algorithmic foundation, our analysis notes that these frameworks rely on provisional complexity-theoretic assumptions that remain vulnerable to future quantum algorithmic advancements. Furthermore, by translating this cryptographic mechanism into physical thermodynamics, we illustrate that intentionally injected discrete Gaussian noise does not equate to the permanent erasure of information. Because the structural integrity of the cryptographic secret remains preserved within the ciphertext, advanced quantum error correction protocols and quantum learning models can efficiently extract the underlying mathematical kernel. Ultimately, we suggest that while lattice-based cryptography provides a robust transitional alternative, definitively classifying these frameworks as unconditionally post-quantum represents a premature classification relying on transient physical bottlenecks rather than impenetrable theoretical boundaries.

sources.title: Intent-Based Cryptographic API Design for Cryptographic Agility
sources.abstract: As organizations move toward post-quantum cryptography, they face the major challenge of updating cryptographic algorithms across large, complex software portfolios. However, most cryptographic APIs in use today were designed around specific algorithms. These APIs expect explicit use of specific algorithms, provide little or no support for policy-based algorithm selection, and offer no straightforward way to migrate existing keys to newer algorithms. This makes the transition to post-quantum cryptography challenging. The companion assessment framework identifies the barriers to cryptographic agility and explains why algorithm transition is largely a software engineering problem. To address the limitations of current cryptographic APIs, we identify the principles necessary to design a cryptographically agile API. The design principles are derived from five fundamental architectural characteristics (Abstraction, Stability, Temporal Flexibility, Separation, and Extensibility). We also show how the design principles can be implemented using several examples of Protocol Buffers API design patterns. In particular, we present an intent vocabulary that is based on scopes which allows for decoupling key creation from algorithm identities. It also supports transparent substitutions of algorithms in the applicable scope. Cryptographic governance is enabled by an abstract policy API that does not prescribe the policy format. Keys are represented by stable identifiers and support key evolution operations (rotation, transformation, migration), facilitating migration between algorithms and providers while tracking both the original key identity and its evolution history. With this approach, updating cryptography becomes an operational process without the need to rewrite application code.

sources.venue: International Conference on Cybersecurity and Digital Defense (ICyDD)

sources.title: Layered Cryptographic Trust for Open Digital Systems: A Conceptual Framework Linking Private-Key Limitations, Public-Key Exchange and Post-Quantum Migration
sources.abstract: Modern digital infrastructures rely on cryptography to establish confidentiality, integrity, authentication, non-repudiation and secure key establishment over networks that cannot be assumed trustworthy. Yet the relationship between private-key limitations, public-key exchange, computational security, pseudorandomness, chosen-plaintext security and post-quantum migration is often presented in fragmented form. This study develops a layered design-science framework for cryptographic trust in open digital systems. The work adopts a conceptual review method supported by standards-based triangulation. Core techniques were analysed against their security role, mathematical basis, computing requirements, application domain, operational risk and post-quantum relevance. The resulting framework shows that symmetric encryption remains the most practical mechanism for high-volume data protection, but it depends on reliable key establishment and lifecycle governance. Public-key cryptography provides scalable trust and authentication, while Diffie-Hellman exchange and key derivation functions connect mathematical shared-secret construction to deployable session keys. Pseudorandomness and chosen-plaintext security give formal discipline to encryption design, whereas post-quantum cryptography introduces migration requirements for long-term confidentiality and identity assurance. The study contributes an integrated architecture that connects cryptographic theory, implementation practice and institutional readiness. Its main implication is that secure systems should be designed as hybrid, lifecycle-aware and algorithm-agile infrastructures rather than as isolated deployments of individual cryptographic primitives.

sources.title: A Review of the Post-Quantum Cryptographic Landscape
sources.venue: International journal of high school research
sources.abstract: As the development of quantum computing systems advances, the integrity of current public-key and symmetrickey cryptographic systems, such as RSA, ECC, and AES, faces unprecedented threats.These systems rely on mathematical problems like integer factorization and discrete logarithms, which quantum algorithms like Shor's can solve exponentially faster than classical ones.This review examines the vulnerability of widely used cryptographic systems and evaluates how close quantum hardware is to breaching real-world encryption.It also discusses the development of post-quantum cryptographic algorithms, specifically lattice-based, code-based, and multivariate polynomial systems designed to resist quantum attacks.This paper will also assess the strengths, limitations, and standardization progress of these post-quantum solutions to provide an understanding of the modern cryptographic landscape.

sources.title: Securing Digital Communications: Quantum and Post-Quantum Cryptography
sources.venue: Journal of Electrical and Computational Innovations
sources.abstract: As quantum computing advances toward practical use, classical cryptography is at a serious risk of being compromised, especially with the use of quantum algorithms like the Shor algorithm, which can break RSA in polynomial time, as well as Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC). This research paper highlights the urgent need to protect electronic communications against quantum attacks by leveraging two novel approaches: Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) and Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC). The study aims to evaluate the effectiveness, scalability, and integration possibility of these technologies separately and in mixed combinations, to achieve long-term resilient cybersecurity. This research is a mixed-methods study that combines literature analysis, expert surveys, and performance benchmarking to determine the strength of encryption, compatibility with the network, and feasibility in the real world. First-hand information was gathered through structured surveys among cybersecurity professionals and scholars. In contrast, second-hand information was retrieved from peer-reviewed journals and official standards of institutions, such as NIST. It has been found that QKD offers unparalleled information-theoretic security, founded on quantum mechanics, yet has limitations in terms of scale and cost. PQC algorithms, however, especially lattice-based cryptography, are simpler to integrate into a classical infrastructure but present a performance issue on hardware with limited capabilities. Based on the study, a hybridized cryptographic model appears to be the best solution to the current approach of implementing the secure key exchange properties of QKD and the universal properties of PQC, without compromising either.

sources.title: Hybrid Keys in Practice: Combining Classical, Quantum and Post-Quantum Cryptography
sources.abstract: Currently, with the threat of quantum computer attacks, the idea of combining several same-type primitives has reemerged. This is also the case for cryptographic keys where a hybrid quantum key exchange combination allows for preserving the security guarantees of pre-quantum schemes and achieving quantum resistance of post-quantum schemes. In this article, we present a concrete 3-key combiner system implemented on a Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGA) platform. Our system involves a pre-quantum Key EXchange scheme (KEX), a post-quantum key encapsulation mechanism, and a Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) algorithm. The proposed 3-key combiner is proven to be secure in the quantum standard model and it is INDistinguishable under a Chosen-Ciphertext Attack (IND-CCA). Our combiner can run in small FPGA platforms due to its relatively low resources usage. In particular, the key combiner without QKD is able to output up to 1 624 keys per second and the key combiner with QKD is able to output up to 9.2 keys per second.

sources.title: Fortifying Future IoT Security: A Comprehensive Review on Lightweight Post-Quantum Cryptography
sources.abstract: This paper presents lightweight Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC), identifying its importance for a shift from traditional cryptographic schemes, vulnerable to quantum threats, to efficient PQC algorithms. Lattice-based cryptography stands out owing to its small key sizes and computational efficiency, with CRYSTALS-Kyber and NTRU algorithms being substantial representatives for Internet of Things (IoT) applications. However, PQC implementation in IoT environments has various obstacles to overcome. Minimizing energy consumption, scalability, and hardware limitations remain key challenges for PQC smooth integration into these resource-constrained networks. The present review analyzes the state-of-the-art PQC, makes security and performance comparisons among leading algorithms, and evaluates optimization techniques aimed at reducing resource overheads. Algorithmic refinement, hardware acceleration, and hybrid cryptography are also discussed as methods for mitigating these challenges. The results indicate that continuous research and development efforts should be made to improve the PQC technologies, and thus achieve their practical deployment in IoT systems. Quantum threats in IoT will be, hence, prevented with the employment of secure and scalable IoT ecosystems in a post-quantum world.

sources.title: Post-quantum cryptographic authentication protocol for industrial IoT using lattice-based cryptography
sources.abstract: The integration of NIST-standardized lattice-based cryptographic algorithms (ML-KEM and ML-DSA) into TLS 1.3 enables post-quantum secure authentication for Industrial IoT (IIoT) environments. This work implements these algorithms within the X.509 certificate infrastructure and evaluates their performance on resource-constrained IIoT hardware (Raspberry Pi 4). Experimental measurements covering key generation, encapsulation, decapsulation, and signature operations were obtained using a liboqs-enabled TLS 1.3 stack. The results show that PQ TLS 1.3 achieves comparable handshake latency to conventional TLS on IIoT-class gateways, with certificate size identified as the dominant overhead. These findings confirm the practicality of post-quantum authentication in IIoT systems while acknowledging limitations related to the hardware scope and simulated networking. Future work will extend validation to field deployments and additional PQC candidates.

sources.title: Post-Quantum Cryptography: Designing Secure Cryptographic Systems to Withstand the Threat of Quantum Computing Attacks
sources.abstract: The emergence of quantum computing poses a serious threat to traditional communication systems, endangering the security of digital communications and critical infrastructure. Although existing cryptographic algorithms (such as RSA and ECC) rely on the inefficiency of computing large numbers or solving logarithm inequality problems, quantum algorithms (especially Shor's algorithm) can solve these problems efficiently. To mitigate this threat, the field of post-quantum cryptography (PQC) has emerged and focuses on developing cryptographic systems that are resilient to quantum attacks. The main techniques in PQC include lattice-based, hash-based, code-based, and multivariate polynomial cryptography. Lattice-based cryptography is the leading contender, providing high security and supporting good properties such as fully homomorphic encryption, but facing issues related to size and computational efficiency. Hash-based encryption enables strong digital signatures but has limitations. Code-based encryption based on error-correcting codes provides proof of security but requires small size. Multivariate polynomial cryptography has good performance but has drawbacks in some applications. While standardization efforts led by organizations such as NIST continue, PQC is at the forefront of protecting the digital future from the impact of quantum computing, ensuring the integrity and confidentiality of information in the post-quantum era.

sources.title: Assessing Readiness of Organization for Post-Quantum Cryptography [US20260352575A1]
sources.abstract: [0000]    Systems and methods are provided for analyzing and defining the readiness or preparedness of a network infrastructure to transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) operation. In one implementation, a method includes a step of collecting information with respect to a current state of a network infrastructure associated with an organization, wherein the collected information is related to compliance of the network infrastructure with PQC standards. The method further includes a step of calculating a PQC readiness score from the collected information. Next, the method includes displaying, on a User Interface (UI), the PQC readiness score and one or more recommended remediation actions for improving the PQC readiness score.

sources.title: METHOD AND SYSTEM FOR STRATEGIZING NETWORK MIGRATION IN ADAPTATION TO POST QUANTUM CRYPTOGRAPHY [EP4835707A1]
sources.abstract: With the advancements in quantum computing, transitioning to quantum-safe cryptography is becoming increasingly critical to keep today's network secure. The present disclosure introduces a method for industrial application network migration. This involves formalizing a Harvest Now Decrypt Later (HNDL) adversarial model, finding a risk score of a successful HNDL attack in any network links followed by in any network component. Graph theory and the Markov chain is used for finding out the central network points. The centrality of network points is measured using a centrality score. The central points are the points in the network, compromising those can compromise a significant part of the total network. Finally, a critical score is given to network points based on risk score, centrality score and metadata about the network points. This critical score can be a priority number given to the network points to rank them for migration to quantum safe state.

sources.title: POST-QUANTUM CRYPTOGRAPHY USING HIGH-MEMORY MASKED CONVOLUTIONAL CODES WITH DUAL-LAYER ERROR MECHANISMS [WO2026224702A1]
sources.abstract: A cryptographic encryption system for securing communications resistant to quantum computing attacks. The sender processes a plaintext vector by computing a remainder polynomial and appending its coefficients to form an augmented vector, multiplies the augmented vector by a public key derived from a masked convolutional code, and introduces random errors into the resulting ciphertext sufficient to increase cryptanalytic resistance while maintaining decodability, thereby generating an error-injected ciphertext. The recipient recovers the plaintext by applying an inverse permutation to the error-injected ciphertext, generating candidate unmasked vectors by subtracting possible masking vectors, performing polynomial division on constituent polynomials of each candidate to form candidate decoded vectors, applying parallel Viterbi decoding to identify the most likely codeword, transforming the codeword using an inverse transformation matrix, verifying the result using a predetermined error detection polynomial, and extracting the plaintext vector.

sources.title: STABLECOIN ECOSYSTEM WITH MULTI-ASSET COLLATERAL, AI-GOVERNED MONETARY POLICY, POST-QUANTUM CRYPTOGRAPHY, AND INTEGRATED UGC LICENSING [WO2026222126A1]
sources.abstract: The present invention pertains to a blockchain-based stablecoin ecosystem integrating Al-driven monetary policy, algorithmically managed multi-asset reserves, tranche-segmented liquidity, decentralized oracle- verified proof-of-reserve, Al-augmented governance, NTT-based licensing with stablecoin royalty micropayments, a threshold-signature cross-chain lock-and-mint bridge, a user-centric wallet payment-rails interface, a content creator-economy SDK, and a crypto-agile quantum-resistant security framework. The modules cooperate to maintain price stability, ensure transparent and fully backed cross-chain circulation, enable creator monetization, facilitate mainstream payment integration, and provide consumer loyalty rewards, thereby addressing known shortcomings of existing single-asset or algorithmic stablecoins on Ethereum and other blockchain networks while extending the stablecoin's utility into everyday commerce.

sources.title: EDGE NEURAL PROCESSING UNIT WITH INTEGRATED POST-QUANTUM CRYPTOGRAPHY HARDWARE ACCELERATION AND QUANTUM-INSPIRED OPTIMIZATION AND OPERATING METHOD THEREOF [KR103034417B1]
DNS+ protocol and infrastructure for enhanced domain utility [US12756557B1]
sources.abstract: A secure, field-based data sharing protocol leveraging the DNS infrastructure with DNSSEC, post-quantum cryptography, and real-time usability flows. The protocol enables domain owners to selectively expose structured confidential data (e.g., IBANs, credit cards, wallets, phone numbers) to authorized entities like banks, PSPs, or telcos using a set of predictable, encrypted DNS TXT records. It introduces a format for revocable, auditable, and verifiable publishing of confidential information, distributed without centralized APIs.

sources.title: SECURE DEVICE REGISTRATION [US20260300468A1]
sources.abstract: One embodiment provides a method, the method including: receiving, from a device of a user, a request to register a second device with a computing system, wherein the second device includes at least one post-quantum cryptography key corresponding to the computing system; generating, at the computing system, a registration token for the second device, wherein the registration token includes a random string of characters and is encapsulated using at least one post-quantum cryptography key corresponding to the second device; transmitting, from the computing system, the registration token to the device of the user, wherein the device of the user transmits the registration token to the second device; and validating, at the computing system, a registration response received at the computing system from the device of the user, wherein the registration response is generated by the second device and transmitted to the device of the user.

sources.title: METHODS AND APPARATUS FOR END-TO-END WTRU-NF SECURITY POLICY MANAGEMENT WITH PQC PROTECTION [US20260304112A1]
sources.abstract: [0000]    A method may be implemented by a wireless transmit/receive unit (WTRU), including sending, to a network, a protocol data unit (PDU) session establishment request, which may include an indication of a network function (NF) intent and security requirements. NF-specific security policies (NFSSPs) may be received from the network in response to the PDU session establishment request. The NFSSPs may be associated with a target NF instance. The NFSSPs may be determined to be valid NFSSPs based on a signature associated with each of the NFSSPs. Post-quantum cryptography (PQC) algorithms may be determined based on the valid NFSSPs or WTRU context information. End-to-end communication may be performed with the target NF instance based on the valid NFSSPs using the PQC algorithms. A security monitoring report may be sent to the network and may be based on a WTRU security monitoring report policy for each of the valid NFSSPs.

sources.title: NTT ML-KEM Apparatus and Method for ML-KEM Post-Quantum Cryptography Operation Based on a Reconfigurable NTT Module [KR103012983B1]
Post quantum cryptography chip, digital signature method, equipment and medium [CN122640125A]
sources.abstract: The invention discloses a post quantum cryptography chip, a digital signature method, equipment and a medium, and relates to the technical field of information security, the post quantum cryptography chip comprises a control module, an operation module and an AHB bus; the control module is used for receiving and analyzing a decoding instruction issued by the AHB to obtain an input seed; the operation module is used for performing hash operation on an input seed, generating a pseudo-random byte stream, writing the pseudo-random byte stream into the shared FIFO buffer, dividing the pseudo-random byte stream in the buffer into two paths of data, performing parallel pipeline sampling on the two paths of data, inputting two paths of sampling results into the ping-pong FIFO buffer, and outputting the two paths of sampling results into the ping-pong FIFO buffer; and performing polynomial operation on the two paths of sampling results by utilizing a Dillithium algorithm to obtain target polynomial data for executing a target password operation task. According to the invention, the resource consumption of the cryptographic chip can be reduced, the hardware cost and the chip area are reduced, and the chip resource utilization rate is improved.

sources.title: Vehicle control data transmission method and vehicle [CN122640115A]
sources.organization: ANHUI KAIYANG TECH CO LTD, CHERY AUTOMOBILE CO LTD
sources.abstract: The embodiment of the invention provides a vehicle control data transmission method and a vehicle, and relates to the technical field of vehicles. The method comprises the following steps: receiving digital key information sent by a terminal through an REE module; receiving an encrypted digital key from the terminal through the TEE module under the condition that the digital key information indicates that the terminal has the post quantum password encryption capability; decrypting the encrypted digital key through the TEE module to obtain the digital key; and verifying the quantum digital signature and the operation authority through the TEE module, and outputting an operation instruction corresponding to the operation request after the verification is passed. A post quantum cryptography encryption algorithm is adapted to a vehicle machine processor, so that a vehicle adopts a quantum encryption mode for encryption during data transmission, and the purpose of effectively preventing quantum attacks is achieved; therefore, the technical problem that the security is poor in the vehicle control data transmission process due to the fact that quantum attacks cannot be effectively prevented by adopting a traditional public key password in the related technology is solved.

sources.title: AI FPGA AI-based Threat Detection and Blockchain Smart Contract-enabled FPGA Post-Quantum Cryptography Security Communication System [KR20260126063A]
Digital testament security management method and system based on artificial intelligence, block chain, distributed storage and post quantum cryptography [CN122595344A]
sources.abstract: The invention discloses a digital testament security management method and system based on artificial intelligence, a block chain, distributed storage and post quantum cryptography, and belongs to the technical field of crossing of computer software, information security, block chain evidence storage, distributed storage and artificial intelligence. In order to solve the problems of high long-term security risk, imperfect evidence storage architecture, lack of process management, weak intelligent assistance and the like of an existing testament system, the invention provides a comprehensive technical scheme: a lattice-based certificateless public key encryption is adopted to guarantee the long-term confidentiality of the testament; collaborative evidence storage is realized by storing the ciphertext under the IPFS chain and anchoring the CID on the alliance chain; constructing a closed-loop process of controlling testament from creation, auditing, notarization, confirmation to effectiveness by a full-life-cycle state machine; performing semantic pre-auditing by using a large language model in combination with legal rules; and key operation authority control is realized through private key hash verification. The scheme is suitable for the fields of digital testament management, heritage planning and legal science and technology services.

sources.title: Identity authentication access system and method based on post-quantum hybrid signature and authorization code [CN122601212A]
sources.abstract: The invention discloses an identity authentication access system and method based on a post-quantum hybrid signature and an authorization code, and belongs to the technical field of information security. The method aims at solving the problems that an existing OAuth 2.0 authorization framework lacks anti-quantum computing capacity, post quantum cryptography migration is difficult, and the safety of an equipment authorization process is insufficient. The system comprises a key management module used for storing a classic signature key pair and a post-quantum signature key pair; the authorization server is used for generating a mixed signature JWT and supporting an equipment authorization code process; and the API gateway is used for carrying out double signature verification on the mixed signature JWT and forwarding the extracted declaration information to a downstream service through an HTTP request header. The external format of the generated mixed signature JWT is completely consistent with that of the standard JWT, and the compatibility with an existing system is kept; the post-quantum signature is verified in a centralized manner through the API gateway, and the declaration is forwarded, so that the post-quantum migration cost of the service system is remarkably reduced. The method can be widely applied to identity authentication and Internet of Things equipment authorization scenes needing anti-quantum security.

sources.title: Unmanned aerial vehicle key distribution method and system based on post quantum cryptography [CN122578158A]
sources.abstract: The invention belongs to the technical field of unmanned aerial vehicle cluster communication security, and relates to an unmanned aerial vehicle key distribution method and system based on post quantum cryptography, and the method comprises the steps: obtaining a post quantum key packaging ciphertext stream, analyzing a memory structure, and carrying out the stripping to obtain a common algebraic matrix and a node feature vector of a member node in a corresponding cluster; constructing a sensing matrix reflecting cluster space topology and channel bandwidth capacity; the method comprises the following steps: establishing asymmetric mapping logic of a common algebraic matrix and a node feature vector on a physical channel, delivering the common algebraic matrix to an omnidirectional low-frequency multicast channel, and routing the node feature vector to a directional high-frequency channel. The retransmission redundancy of the common load in the cluster key distribution process is eliminated, the broadcast storm caused by a large-volume ciphertext in a dynamic fading channel is solved, and the convergence speed of a security protocol in a severe channel environment is improved.

sources.title: Post-quantum cryptography signature decoding method and device, equipment and storage medium [CN122578172A]
sources.abstract: The invention discloses a post quantum cryptography signature decoding method and device, equipment and a storage medium, and relates to the technical field of data processing, and the method comprises the steps: reading to-be-decoded signature data from a first memory according to a preset bit width through a preset decoding state machine; in a fixed segment decoding state, extracting symbol information and fixed length numerical value information according to a byte granularity stream; entering a variable length segment decoding state, searching an end flag bit in parallel according to byte granularity, and determining variable length coding numerical value information; and performing reduction according to the symbol information, the fixed-length numerical value information and the variable-length coding numerical value information to obtain a current polynomial coefficient, and writing the current polynomial coefficient into a second memory according to a preset bit width so as to perform signature verification. Therefore, stream extraction is combined with state machine control, so that complete restoration from variable-length coding to a fixed-length coefficient can be ensured; meanwhile, the search granularity of an end flag bit is improved to be byte-level parallel processing, so that the decoding period of a single polynomial coefficient can be reduced; therefore, the compression decoding time consumption can be effectively shortened.

sources.title: NTT acceleration method and device based on dual-prime CRT in post quantum cryptography and storage medium [CN122554073A]
authors: BEIJING LANGKONG QUANTUM TECH CO LTD
sources.organization: BEIJING LANGKONG QUANTUM TECH CO LTD
sources.abstract: The invention belongs to the technical field of post-quantum cryptography and information security, and relates to a dual-prime CRT-based NTT acceleration method and device in post-quantum cryptography and a storage medium, and the method comprises the steps: reading preset prime number parameters, selecting a first prime number and a second prime number, and storing the first prime number and the second prime number in a readable storage medium; obtaining a first input polynomial and a second input polynomial, and performing reduction to obtain a reduced polynomial pair; pre-calculating a fusion constant table, loading the reduced polynomial to a vector register, carrying out forward number-theory transformation to obtain a frequency domain point value corresponding to a polynomial pair, reading the frequency domain point value representation corresponding to the polynomial pair, carrying out point-by-point multiplication to obtain a frequency domain product polynomial, carrying out reverse number-theory transformation to obtain a time domain product polynomial; performing point-by-point merging reconstruction on the term coefficient sequence corresponding to the time domain product polynomial to obtain a target product polynomial; the technical problems that in the prior art, calculation complexity is too high, and performance improvement is limited are solved.

sources.title: Digital signature reinforcement method and system for lattice password sampling rejection and medium thereof [CN122554105A]
authors: BEIJING LANGKONG QUANTUM TECH CO LTD
sources.organization: BEIJING LANGKONG QUANTUM TECH CO LTD
sources.abstract: The invention discloses a digital signature reinforcement method and system for lattice password sampling rejection and a medium thereof, and belongs to the technical field of post quantum cryptography. The method comprises the following steps: configuring a plurality of redundant state variables, endowing an anti-compiler with an optimization attribute, and forcing a microprocessor to directly initiate a read-write transaction to a physical memory; calling an underlying verification module to carry out multiple independent evaluation and storing each state variable; carrying out aggregation calculation on the plurality of state variables by adopting a bitwise logic operator of non-short-circuit evaluation; and releasing the signature only when the aggregation result shows that all the evaluation values do not cross the boundary, or else erasing the intermediate state and re-triggering the signature cycle. By means of software and hardware collaborative design, on the premise that expensive hardware sensors are not added, fault injection attacks and compiler optimization are resisted at the same time, and the method has the constant time characteristic and can be used for safety equipment such as intelligent cards and financial gateways.

sources.title: Anti-quantum-attack AI security chip architecture and method [CN122528222A]
sources.abstract: The invention discloses an AI security chip architecture and method for resisting quantum attacks. The chip is integrated with a quantum cryptography hardware acceleration engine, a hybrid certificate chain verification unit, a physical intrusion detection and self-destruction unit, an ultralow temperature self-destruction locking unit and a runtime memory integrity measurement unit. The post quantum cryptography hardware acceleration engine comprises a reconfigurable logic unit and supports dynamic adaptation of NIST follow-up PQC standards through secure microcode updating; the mixed certificate chain verification ensures smooth transition of the traditional password system; a distributed capacitance sensing grid and a chip are integrally manufactured in the same manufacturing process to actively sense physical invasion; the final state signal is encrypted and sent, and the local record supports an evidence obtaining mode or is automatically destroyed after sending; the ultralow-temperature locking unit dynamically determines a threshold value based on electrolyte characteristics of a current chip manufacturing process; the anti-combination attack logic directly triggers irreversible self-destruction when the physical invasion and the ultralow temperature are triggered at the same time. The problems that an existing AI security chip cannot resist quantum computing attacks at the same time, physical intrusion protection is insufficient, self-destruction can be bypassed in an extreme environment, and combined attack prevention capacity is lacked are solved.

sources.title: Double-track reconfigurable post-quantum cryptography processing method and device compatible with international standard and storage medium [CN122513078A]
authors: BEIJING LANGKONG QUANTUM TECH CO LTD
sources.organization: BEIJING LANGKONG QUANTUM TECH CO LTD
sources.abstract: The invention discloses a double-track reconfigurable post-quantum cryptography processing method and device compatible with an international standard and a storage medium. The processing method comprises the steps of dynamically configuring a standard track mode or a high-defense track mode of a reconfigurable computing array according to an upper-layer handshake protocol instruction; according to the method, an interconnection network is configured to be a global butterfly cross topology, and polynomial operation based on prime number analog is executed; according to the local two-dimensional grid topology, the interconnection network is configured to be a local two-dimensional grid topology, addition-multiplication global mixed blinding is executed for the modulus, and local short convolution operation is completed through multi-phase decomposition; the same spread spectrum multi-phase interleaving clock network provides time sequence driving for the bottom layer pipeline registers of the two modes. According to the invention, a bottom layer multiplication and addition unit is multiplexed at a transistor level, nanosecond-level switching of number-theory transformation and a systolic array is realized through routing reconstruction, undifferentiated physical energy spreading protection is carried out on double tracks by using a spread spectrum multiphase interleaving clock, and the technical contradiction between standard compliance and limit physical defense is overcome.
